turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Please come in, madam. I just checked her — pulse is ninety-eight, blood pressure one hundred and ten over seventy... sorry, that was the wrong reading, it is one hundred and eight over sixty-eight, and oxygen saturation is ninety-seven percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. I am Dr. Iyer. Sit comfortably. What has been bothering you?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, actually I am just very tired. I teach class four at St. Mary's, and by the second period itself my legs feel heavy, and when I reach home I don't even feel like checking copies, though my husband thinks I have become lazy, which is not fair.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tiredness, I hear you. Are you getting short of breath as well, or is it the weakness only?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): The school day is very long, you know, assembly then four periods before lunch, and the stairs to the staff room are quite steep, and I...
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She stops halfway, doctor. I am her mother, Latha, I came with her. At home also she sits after one flight.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, sorry, I trailed off. I get breathless when I climb stairs or walk fast to the bus. When I am sitting and teaching I am okay, not gasping or anything.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. How long has the tiredness been there, and the breathlessness?

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): The weakness has been there for quite some time, I cannot give one neat date. The breathlessness I was going to say six weeks... no, actually closer to two months, it started around the unit tests.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weakness plus breathlessness on exertion, and the pulse is a bit fast. I am already wondering about the blood. Tell me about your periods — have they been heavy?

[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): That is the main thing, I should have started there. For one year the flow has been very heavy. On the heavy days I change the pad many times, four or five, sometimes more, I don't sit and count properly, and there are clots also.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One year she says. Doctor, it is more than that. After her brother's wedding, nearly two years now, she has been complaining about this bleeding.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I will not force one number. Let us keep it as somewhere between one and two years of heavy bleeding. The clots — how big are we talking?

[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Not enormous, doctor. Sometimes like a one-rupee coin, sometimes bigger than that, I cannot describe it exactly, they just come and I get worried, and I have never measured them.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding between the periods, or pain that keeps you in bed?

[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Between periods, no, it stops cleanly. Pain is only mild cramps, nothing like what I had before my deliveries. I have two children, both normal delivery, the younger is six now.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, mild cramps only, no bleeding in between. Any other change you have noticed in yourself?
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her hair, doctor, please ask. The bathroom drain is full of hair. And in our family thyroid is there — I myself am on thyroid tablets.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): One thing at a time. Hair loss — is that true?

[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, when I comb, so much hair comes out. When it started I cannot say exactly, somewhere in the last few months, four or five maybe, there is no particular date in my mind.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any feeling of being unusually cold, constipation, or weight gain? I am thinking aloud — hair, tiredness, and thyroid in the mother, hypothyroidism can sit in this picture, though I am not deciding yet.

[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Weight is the same only, I checked on the school scale last week. Constipation, no. Cold, I don't think so, Chennai is hot anyway, I am not sitting with a shawl or anything.

[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I take thyroxine, seventy-five micrograms... no, my doctor put it up, it is hundred micrograms now. That is my tablet, not hers. And her sister Meena takes biotin for hair fall, those small tablets. Priya swallowed one of them once and then left it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will not put your thyroxine or Meena's biotin on Priya's list. Priya, which tablets are you actually taking?

[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Iron. I almost said folic acid, but that was only during pregnancy, years back, I stopped it after that. Now it is ferrous sulphate. I thought the strip said two hundred milligrams... no, I looked this morning, it is three twenty-five milligrams.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): And how often do you actually take it?

[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): The doctor I saw earlier said one tablet daily, by mouth, for this weakness. But sometimes only. I forget when I am rushing. Maybe two or three days in a week — I cannot be sure I am taking it the way he said.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the plan on paper is daily, and the real life is patchy. I will not change the tablet today until we see the numbers. Please try to take that three twenty-five by mouth once a day, with a little food if the stomach complains.

[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): If I take it daily I get black stools and some nausea, so I skip, that is the honest reason. It is not severe, just uncomfortable, and then I think I will restart tomorrow and tomorrow never comes.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood, we can talk about a gentler preparation after the bloods if needed. Any chest pain, fever, or giddiness along with the breathlessness?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Last week during annual day practice I was standing in the corridor for ages, the children were shouting, and I thought maybe the heat was...

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Sorry, that is not what you asked. Chest pain, no. Fever, no. A little giddiness when I stand up quickly, yes, more on the heavy period days. On Sunday in the kitchen I felt I might fall, but I held the counter.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good that you caught yourself. Let me examine you. Conjunctiva is pale, and the tongue is pale too. I am not hearing any murmur, heart sounds are normal, though the rate feels fast, same as that pulse. Lungs are clear, no creps.

[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Is it the heart, doctor? My neighbour had a heart problem and she was breathless, and I keep comparing, which I know is not logical. I even tried counting my pulse with the phone at night, but the number was jumping and I don't trust it.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't think this is primarily the heart, and I won't use a phone reading we both don't trust. Putting it together — heavy bleeding for roughly one to two years, tiredness, breathlessness on stairs, looking pale, pulse fast — my working impression is iron deficiency anaemia from the menorrhagia. Hypothyroidism is still possible, I cannot rule it out with your mother's history, but I am not confirming that today.

[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): So what is the next step? I can come any day except Thursday, that is the PTA meeting, and Friday I have substitution duty, but if you tell me the day I will speak to my principal, she is usually understanding if I inform her before.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood tests first. I am ordering a full blood count, that includes the haemoglobin, plus serum ferritin, and a TSH. Those I am booking today, not maybe.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the samples once you are done, doctor, if she has a few minutes. She has not fasted, will that be a problem?
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Haemoglobin, ferritin and TSH do not need fasting. Yes, please draw them today, two tubes is enough.

[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): I had coffee only, no breakfast, I was rushing to get the auto. If it matters I can eat at the canteen downstairs and come back up, it is just near the pharmacy, they make decent idli.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): No need to eat first. About a pelvic scan, I am not sending you today. If the bleeding stays this heavy, or the haemoglobin comes back very low, then we might do a pelvic ultrasound. It is not booked now.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should she stop the iron before the test? I read somewhere on the phone that iron can change the result, I don't know if that is correct.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't stop it. Keep trying for once a day if the stomach allows, and at review tell me how many doses you truly managed. We can still read the ferritin.

[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): And if I feel worse at home? At night I sometimes wake and start counting my breaths, which is silly, I know, my mind just runs, and then I cannot tell if I am actually worse or only frightened.

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you soak a pad every hour for several hours, or you are breathless even while resting, or you faint, go to emergency the same day. Otherwise I want to see you back in two weeks with these reports.

[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine. Should I bring my husband? He is on metformin for his sugar, five hundred milligrams twice a day, and he keeps saying I should get checked, but his sugar problem is his, not mine.
[SEG0047] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And my thyroid you have written, no? I am hypothyroid for ten years. Priya's thyroid was never tested, that is why I pushed her to come.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted — mother with hypothyroidism — and that is exactly why her TSH is on the form. I am not putting any confirmed label on her today. The bloods will talk.

[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): One more thing, sorry, I keep adding details. Sleep is broken on the heavy days because I get up to change the pad, but other nights I sleep fine. Appetite is normal, rice and sambar as usual, maybe a little less if the iron makes me queasy, but generally I am eating.

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Broken sleep only on the heavy days, appetite otherwise alright. I am not going to chase diet or anything else we have not touched. Sister will draw the blood now, and reception can give you the two-week slot.
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): Come along, madam, it is only two tubes. If you feel giddy while I am drawing, just say, I will lie you flat.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay. Ma, hold my bag so I don't forget the iron strip — if they ask the strength again, it is three twenty-five, I checked, not two hundred. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): You are welcome. We will go through the numbers together in two weeks, and only then decide if the scan is actually needed.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Husband's sugar is not family history of the patient.
Giddiness on standing quickly/heavy days is supported; 'mild' severity is not stated.
bad.text: giddiness on standing (category=neurological, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, aggravating_factors=standing up quickly; heavy period days, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Drug, dose, route, indication, current use supported; actual frequency is patchy, not confirmed once daily.
bad.text: ferrous sulphate (generic_name=ferrous sulfate, dose=325 mg, route=oral, frequency=once daily, indication=weakness, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Current ferrous sulphate adherence and tolerance details are incomplete: although prescribed 325 mg orally once daily, she actually takes it only about 2 to 3 days per week because daily use causes black stools and some nausea; this is the honest reason she skips doses.
Negative finding not recorded: no pain severe enough to keep her in bed; menstrual pain is only mild cramps.
Negative finding not recorded: weight is unchanged/same, not just no weight gain.
History not recorded: two children, both delivered normally; younger child is six years old.

Planned investigation logistics not recorded: blood samples were to be drawn the same day and fasting was not required for haemoglobin/full blood count, ferritin, and TSH; doctor specified two tubes would be enough.

Red-flag advice is incomplete/misstated: the doctor advised emergency care if she faints, not just for 'fainting' as a general concept but if it occurs at home along with the other warning signs; also the threshold was soaking a pad every hour for several hours.
Follow-up detail not recorded: at review she should report how many iron doses she truly managed to take.
